records.source: הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ׀אוֹדֶ֣ה יְ֭הוָה בְּכָל־לֵבָ֑ב בְּס֖וֹד יְשָׁרִ֣ים וְעֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: Praise Yah! I will give thanks to YHWH with all [the] heart, in [the] council of [the] upright and [the] congregation.
pieces: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! I will thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all my heart where upright people gather, in the whole assembly.

L.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! I will give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all [my] heart, in the council of the upright and [in the] assembly.

R.1: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! I will thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with all my heart when I am with God's people, those who do what is right.

decisions.choice: Praise the LORD: Hallelu-yah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is two words: a plural command, "praise!" (hallelu), and Yah, the short form of the divine name (as in 68:5 and Exodus 15:2). It calls the gathered people to praise. Like the full name, Yah is rendered "the LORD", with Yah as the alternative.

decisions.choice: Psalms 111 and 112: twin alphabet poems
decisions.reason: After the opening "Praise the LORD", which stands outside the pattern, each half line of Psalm 111 begins with the next letter of the Hebrew alphabet, twenty-two lines in all; verses 9 and 10 have three lines each. Psalm 112 is built the same way and repeats its phrases: what this psalm says of the LORD's works, the next says of the person who fears him (compare 111:3 with 112:3, and 111:4 with 112:4).

decisions.choice: council: the close circle of the upright
decisions.reason: The word (sod) is a group gathered in confidence, a circle of friends or counselors. With "congregation" ('edah) it means the gathered people of God.

decisions.choice: God's people, those who do what is right
alternatives: the council of the upright and the congregation
decisions.reason: Readable joins the two words for the gathering into one plain phrase (m3).

records.heading: The great works of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}

records.gloss: Great [are the] works of YHWH, sought out by all who delight in them.
pieces: The deeds of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are great; all who take pleasure in them search them out.

L.2: Great [are] the works of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, sought out by all who delight in them.

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} does great things. Everyone who enjoys them loves to think about them.

decisions.choice: sought out: studied, pondered
decisions.reason: The verb (darash) is to seek, to inquire into. Those who love the LORD's works think about them and search out their meaning.

decisions.choice: works: what the LORD has done for his people
decisions.reason: The works are above all his deeds in Israel's history: the rescue from Egypt, the food in the wilderness, the covenant and the land (verses 4-9).

records.gloss: Splendor and majesty [is] his work, and his righteousness stands forever.
pieces: Everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does shines with splendor and majesty, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness stands for all time.

L.3: Splendor and majesty [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} righteousness stands forever.

R.3: Everything {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does is glorious and wonderful. His righteousness will never end.

decisions.choice: splendor and majesty: the glory of a king
decisions.reason: The pair (hod and hadar) describes royal glory (21:6; 45:4; 96:6). Here it is the glory of what the LORD has done.

decisions.choice: righteousness: his faithfulness in doing what is right
decisions.reason: The LORD's righteousness (tsedaqah) is his acting rightly and faithfully, above all in keeping his covenant and saving his people. 112:3 says the same words of the person who fears him.

records.source: זֵ֣כֶר עָ֭שָׂה לְנִפְלְאֹתָ֑יו חַנּ֖וּן וְרַח֣וּם יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: A remembrance he has made for his wonders; gracious and compassionate [is] YHWH.
pieces: He has set up a memorial of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonderful deeds; {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is gracious and tender in mercy.

L.4: A remembrance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders; gracious and compassionate [is] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: He makes sure that people remember the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is kind and full of mercy.

decisions.choice: made a remembrance: caused his wonders to be remembered
alternatives: made himself a name by his wonders
decisions.reason: The word (zeker) is a memorial, something that keeps a thing in mind. The LORD saw to it that his wonders would be remembered, above all through the festivals, such as the Passover, which was given as "a day of remembrance" (Exodus 12:14).

decisions.choice: gracious and compassionate: the LORD's name in Exodus 34:6
decisions.reason: The LORD described himself to Moses as "compassionate and gracious" (Exodus 34:6); the pair is repeated in 86:15, 103:8 and 145:8. 112:4 uses the same words of the upright.

decisions.choice: He makes sure that people remember
decisions.reason: Readable says what the memorial does (m1).

records.source: טֶ֭רֶף נָתַ֣ן לִֽירֵאָ֑יו יִזְכֹּ֖ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִיתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Food he has given to those who fear him; he remembers forever his covenant.
pieces: He feeds those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and keeps {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant in mind for all time.

L.5: Food {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given to those who fear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembers forever {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant.

R.5: He feeds the people who fear and honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He will never forget the promises of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant.

decisions.choice: food: provision
decisions.reason: The word (teref) is properly prey torn by a wild animal (104:21), and so food. It may recall the manna and quails in the wilderness (Exodus 16).

decisions.choice: fear him: revere him and so obey him
decisions.reason: To fear the LORD is to take him seriously as God: awe that shows itself in trust and obedience (verse 10; 112:1).

decisions.choice: fear and honor
decisions.reason: Readable adds "honor" so that the fear is not taken for terror alone (m2).

decisions.choice: the promises of his covenant
decisions.reason: Readable says what remembering a covenant means: keeping its promises.

records.source: כֹּ֣חַ מַ֭עֲשָׂיו הִגִּ֣יד לְעַמּ֑וֹ לָתֵ֥ת לָ֝הֶ֗ם נַחֲלַ֥ת גּוֹיִֽם׃
records.gloss: [The] power of his works he has declared to his people, to give to them [the] inheritance of nations.
pieces: He made the might of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds known to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them the nations' land to inherit.

L.6: The power of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has declared to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, in giving them the inheritance of [the] nations.

R.6: He showed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people how powerful {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them the land where other nations had lived.

decisions.choice: the inheritance of nations: the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: The LORD gave Israel the land the nations of Canaan had held (Joshua 21:43-45; Deuteronomy 7:1). The gift showed his power.

decisions.choice: declared: made known, shown
decisions.reason: The verb (higgid) is to tell or make known. The LORD made his power known by what he did for his people.

records.source: מַעֲשֵׂ֣י יָ֭דָיו אֱמֶ֣ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֑ט נֶ֝אֱמָנִ֗ים כָּל־פִּקּוּדָֽיו׃
records.gloss: [The] works of his hands [are] faithfulness and justice; reliable [are] all his precepts.
pieces: All that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands do is faithful and just; every one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} precepts can be trusted.

L.7: The works of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hands [are] faithfulness and justice; reliable [are] all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} precepts.

R.7: He is faithful and fair in all that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does. Every one of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions can be relied on.

decisions.choice: faithfulness: truth that can be relied on
decisions.reason: The word ('emet) means firmness: what is true and dependable. His works are as reliable as he is.

decisions.choice: precepts: the charges God lays on his people
decisions.reason: The word (piqqudim) means what someone has been charged to do. It occurs only in the Psalms, most often in Psalm 119.

decisions.choice: instructions
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plainer word, as in Psalm 119.

records.source: סְמוּכִ֣ים לָעַ֣ד לְעוֹלָ֑ם עֲ֝שׂוּיִ֗ם בֶּאֱמֶ֥ת וְיָשָֽׁר׃
records.gloss: Upheld forever, for perpetuity, done in faithfulness and uprightness.
pieces: They stand secure for all time, framed with faithfulness and integrity.

L.8: [They are] upheld forever and ever, done in faithfulness and uprightness.

R.8: They will last forever and ever. They were made with faithfulness and are completely fair.

decisions.choice: they: the precepts of verse 7
decisions.reason: The verse continues the thought of verse 7: the precepts are held firm forever, because they were given faithfully and rightly.

decisions.choice: done: made, or to be carried out
decisions.reason: The form ('asuyim) means "made" or "done". It may say how the precepts were given, or how they are to be kept: faithfully and uprightly.

decisions.choice: They
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the subject the Hebrew leaves implied (m1).

records.source: פְּד֤וּת׀שָׁ֘לַ֤ח לְעַמּ֗וֹ צִוָּֽה־לְעוֹלָ֥ם בְּרִית֑וֹ קָד֖וֹשׁ וְנוֹרָ֣א שְׁמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Redemption he has sent to his people; he has commanded forever his covenant; holy and awesome [is] his name.
pieces: He sent {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people redemption and set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant in place for all time. Holy and awe-inspiring is {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name!

L.9: Redemption {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has sent to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has commanded {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant forever; holy and awesome [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name.

R.9: He set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people free, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made a covenant with them that will last forever. His name is holy, and people should stand in awe of it.

decisions.choice: redemption: setting free
decisions.reason: The word (pedut) is a release, as of a slave bought back. It recalls the LORD's freeing of Israel from Egypt (Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: commanded his covenant: laid it down as binding
decisions.reason: The covenant is not a bargain between equals: the LORD set it in place by his command, and it lasts forever.

decisions.choice: awesome: to be feared
decisions.reason: The word (nora') means "to be feared". It prepares for verse 10: the fear of the LORD.

records.source: רֵ֘אשִׁ֤ית חָכְמָ֨ה׀יִרְאַ֬ת יְהוָ֗ה שֵׂ֣כֶל ט֭וֹבלְכָל־עֹשֵׂיהֶ֑ם תְּ֝הִלָּת֗וֹ עֹמֶ֥דֶת לָעַֽד׃
records.gloss: [The] beginning of wisdom [is the] fear of YHWH; good insight [is] to all who do them; his praise stands forever.
pieces: The fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is where wisdom begins; all who carry them out show good sense. His praise stands for all time.

L.10: The beginning of wisdom [is] the fear of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; good insight [belongs] to all who do them; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise stands forever.

R.10: Wisdom starts with fearing {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and honoring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Everyone who obeys {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instructions shows real understanding. People will praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} forever.

decisions.choice: beginning: the first step and the foundation
decisions.reason: The word (re'shit) is the beginning, and also the first and best part. Wisdom starts from fearing the LORD and rests on it.

decisions.choice: the motto of the wisdom books
decisions.reason: The same saying stands at the head of Proverbs (Proverbs 1:7; 9:10) and in Job 28:28. Here it closes a psalm about the LORD's works and leads into Psalm 112.

decisions.choice: who do them: who keep his precepts
decisions.reason: "Them" is plural and most likely points back to the precepts of verses 7-8.

decisions.choice: his praise: the praise given to the LORD
decisions.reason: "His" is the LORD's: the praise that belongs to him will never end, as his righteousness stands forever (verse 3).

decisions.choice: obeys his instructions
decisions.reason: Readable names what "them" refers to (m3).

decisions.choice: fearing the LORD and honoring him
decisions.reason: As in 111:5.
